katas.title: Two Sum
katas.problem: Given a list of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the two indices i, j (i < j) such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target. Assume exactly one solution exists. Return them as list(i, j).

katas.title: Reverse a list
katas.problem: Return a new list with the elements of the input in reverse order.

katas.title: Valid parentheses
katas.problem: Return true if the string contains a balanced sequence of `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`. Empty input is balanced.

katas.title: Anagram check
katas.problem: Return true if `a` and `b` are anagrams (same letters, same counts). Case-insensitive; ignore spaces.
constraints: Comparison is case-insensitive and ignores spaces.

katas.title: Maximum subarray sum (Kadane)
katas.problem: Return the largest sum of any contiguous subarray. The array is non-empty. Negative numbers are allowed.

katas.title: Move zeros to end
katas.problem: Return a new list where all 0s are moved to the end, preserving the relative order of the non-zero elements.

katas.title: Two-pointer pair sum (sorted)
katas.problem: Given a SORTED list of integers and a target, return list(i, j) (i < j) such that nums[i] + nums[j] == target, or list() if no such pair exists. Use two pointers.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

katas.title: Longest substring without repeating chars
katas.problem: Return the LENGTH of the longest substring of `s` that has no repeated characters. Use a sliding window.

katas.title: Best time to buy and sell stock
katas.problem: Given a list of daily prices, return the maximum profit from a single buy + later sell. Return 0 if no profit is possible.

examples.explanation: Prices only fall, no profitable trade.

katas.title: Climbing stairs (DP)
katas.problem: There are n stairs; you can take 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.

katas.title: Reverse a linked list
katas.problem: Linked-list nodes are dicts: `dict("val", v, "next", node_or_null)`. Given the head, return the new head of the reversed list. Empty input returns null.

katas.title: Binary tree max depth
katas.problem: Tree nodes are dicts: `dict("val", v, "left", l, "right", r)`. Return the maximum depth (number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path). Empty tree (null) has depth 0.

tests.call: max_depth(node(1, node(2, node(3, leaf(4), null), null), null))
